title: structured output: constrained decoding backends - tokenizer & CFG regex edgecases
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Structured-output constrained decoding (CFG/regex) has regressed on a set of tokenizer edgecases introduced by recent tokenization changes. This causes two classes of failures: 1) valid CFG productions being rejected because token boundaries split regex anchors, and 2) permissive regex branches matching unintended tokenized sequences leading to malformed structured outputs. This PR fixes the constrained-decoding backends to handle tokenizer-level anchors and mixed-granularity token boundaries robustly.

Changes in this PR: consolidated CFG matcher entrypoints to use token-aware spans; added a regex preprocessor that normalizes anchor semantics (^, $) to work on token sequences instead of raw bytes; introduced explicit fallback logic for ambiguous token splits (prefer longest token-aligned match unless a CFG production explicitly requires a split); widened unit test coverage for tokenizer edgecases including unicode combining marks, U+200C/ZWNJ, and multibyte punctuation.

Checklist:
- [x] Fix core matcher to operate on token index ranges and not byte offsets
- [x] Add regex->token-sequence normalization and tests
- [x] Add guidance and examples to docs for tokenizer-dependent constraints
- [x] Add integration tests against OpenAI-compat streaming layer to ensure no regressions in tool/function calling flows
- [x] Run perf benchmarks and ensure no >2% regression on 2k token tail latency

Testing: Unit and integration tests added (see files_changed). Manual verification with redwood-eval harness using representative prompts and CFGs. Benchmarks run on internal perf lab; small 0.5-1.5% improvement in common short-sequence cases and <1.8% regression on worst-case pathological token-split CFGs after micro-optimizations.

Migration/compatibility notes: No user-facing API changes. Constraint grammars and regex runtime semantics tightened to be token-aware; existing grammars should continue to work, but grammars depending on byte-level anchors should be adjusted to token anchors if they relied on tokenizer internals. Added docs/examples.

Related: ENG-4512 (structured output robustness), ENG-4601 (tokenizer fixes), SUP-342 (support ticket referencing broken structured outputs).
